text:
emma: Heads-up — after the last load test we're seeing a ton of tiny free fragments on GPU (tensors ~1–8KB) that never get reused and kill our eviction latency. Thinking of a 'granular coalesce' layer in the allocator to merge adjacent tiny frees into larger reclaimable runs before we hand them to the evictor. Thoughts?

raj: Interesting. Are you proposing coalescing at free-time or during background compaction? free-time adds latency on alloc/free path. background avoids tail-latency but needs tracking.

emma: My rough idea: cheap free-time fast-path that records small freed extents in a per-stream bucket (no merge), plus a low-prio coalescer thread that stitches neighbouring extents and promotes them to normal free lists. So normal alloc avoids cost, background compactor improves eviction hits.

mike: How do we detect adjacency on GPU addresses? We need deterministic ordering for ranges, and for MRU pointers across migrations. Also consider fragmentation across multiple CUDA contexts / VMAs.

raj: We already maintain a per-device interval tree keyed by base address. Coalescer could pop from the tiny-bucket and consult the tree to merge adjacent intervals. The tricky part is synchronization — we must avoid races with concurrent allocs and DMA in flight.

emma: Right. I sketched an API for the allocator:

```
// free small chunk fast
alloc.free_small(ptr, size, stream_id);
// background task
alloc.coalesce_worker();
```

Where free_small only inserts a metadata entry; coalesce_worker takes locks and performs merge + moves merged extents into the eviction-ready free list.

raj: That model seems doable. A few tradeoffs:
- coalesce_worker needs to respect pinned/prefetch windows (can't merge ranges pinned by in-flight kernels)
- we should version free entries so if alloc races and reclaims a chunk we can abort merge
- telemetry: expose small_bucket occupancy and coalesce success rate

mike: Also think about CPU offload. If we proactively move tiny tensors to host to reduce GPU fragmentation, we may pay network copy overhead and then eviction churn when they come back. Perhaps only offload big contiguous runs, not 1–8KB stuffs.

emma: Agreed. The coalescer could have a threshold: only merge when total contiguous > 64KB or when small_bucket grows beyond X. Otherwise leave them to be reused by small alloc fast path.

raj: One more thought: for multi-tenant Dedicated pools we should make coalescer optional per-tenant — noisy neighbors might want tighter latency SLOs and avoid background work. Toggle via config: "coalesce_mode": ["off","background","aggressive"].

storage-bot: :warning: eviction: device:gpu0 high fragmentation detected (frag score 0.82) — advised to run coalesce or scale-up.

emma: Nice, that alert lines up with what we saw. Plan: prototype coalescer + metrics in staging (low-prio worker, 64KB threshold, per-device). I'll push RFC doc + benchmark plan.

mike: Can you include a microbenchmark that exercises many tiny alloc/free + background coalesce and measure p95 eviction latency? Also include disabled-coalesce baseline.

raj: I'll review API changes. Need to ensure we don't regress pinned-page accounting and page-locked memory quotas.

emma: Thanks — will send RFC link here when ready. For now low-priority todo: "prototype background coalescer + small_bucket metrics". :+1:
